decisive_question.question: Is the LTM revenue/EBITDA decline a temporary trough tied to the Phase 3.2 capacity ramp that reverses into 2026, or the start of a structural demand/subsidy-driven contraction against an already heavily-levered balance sheet?

evidence_for.claim: Management frames the Q1 revenue dip as temporary, tied to Phase 3.2 ramp timing aligning with customer demand and a continued revenue ramp expected through 2026.

evidence_for.claim: Gross margin held at 35% LTM and absolute EBITDA remains positive (+52), showing the cost structure did not collapse with the volume drop.

evidence_against.claim: Revenue fell -25.5% YoY (latest same-quarter) and EBITDA growth is -66% vs a +2% peer median, with rev growth -9% vs +2% — the contraction is sharper than peers experiencing the same sector.
